gitCommit.subject: feat(sorting): Epic S — Standing usage chip + hand-orderable draft results (mvn5) (#314)
gitCommit.body:
feat(sorting): Epic S — Standing usage chip + hand-orderable draft results (mvn5) (#314)

* docs(specs): Epic S design (rev 2, adversarial review folded) + implementation plan

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UQS4F4JxwFSyyMxHhVdSYz

* feat(results): usage chip on Standing — per-item In your life / Resting annotation (Epic S)

Thread the live usage fold (DecisionController.listForCurator + deriveUsage) into
the Decide/Standing surface and render a quiet, count-free per-item chip — "In
your life" (uses) / "Resting" (not_uses) — on usage-known ranked rows; no chip
when usage is undecided. Extend the render gate so a usage-only collection (usage
answers, no love ranking) shows the item list with chips instead of the empty
state. deriveStanding is unchanged (love-only). DATA-6: only the derived
Map<itemId,answer> is threaded to the client; the raw curator event log stays
server-side.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UQS4F4JxwFSyyMxHhVdSYz

* feat(results): sort_result_items.usage snapshot at materialization + fresh-fold on revision (Epic S)

Add a nullable `usage` text column to sort_result_items (additive migration
0016, no CHECK, no backfill — matches the manualBucket plain-text precedent).
Stamp it at draft materialization from the curator's LIVE usage fold
(loadCuratorDecisionEvents + deriveUsage), threaded through the create-path:
createResultWithItems gains a usageByItemId map and the repo create-input gains
a `usage` field. A usage-unknown item stamps NULL.

Revision uses fresh-fold (§3.3): supersedeResult RE-DERIVES usage from the
CURRENT decision log at revision materialization (the same deriveUsage a fresh
draft runs), so the revision's snapshot describes the revision moment.
cloneItemsFrom stays unchanged — it drops manual overrides and simply does not
carry usage; usage is stamped by the materialization step, not the clone.

The finalized keepsake page reads the snapshot `usage` into the SAME quiet chip
S1 built ("In your life" / "Resting"); a legacy all-NULL result renders none.

Tests: new un-mocked DB integration file proving the migration applied,
per-item stamping (unknown -> NULL), and one revision test asserting BOTH halves
(fresh-folded usage + dropped manual overlay); finalized-page chip render +
legacy-no-chip; existing service/materialization/pipeline suites kept green.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UQS4F4JxwFSyyMxHhVdSYz

* feat(results): transactional bulk re-rank endpoint for draft results (Epic S)

PATCH /api/sort-results/[id]/items applies a whole {rid,manualRank} ordering
in one withTransaction (one drag = one atomic call), and DELETE resets the
manual overlay for every item (back to the computed order). Draft-only (409
finalized), curator-scoped, Zod-validated; every rid is validated against the
result's own items inside the tx so a bad/foreign rid rolls the whole batch
back with a 404. Backs S3b's drag-to-reorder UI.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UQS4F4JxwFSyyMxHhVdSYz

* feat(results): manual re-rank UI — drag + move-up/down on draft results, wired to the bulk endpoint (Epic S)

The DRAFT result page gains a 'Put in order by hand' affordance that flips the
affirmation composition into a flat drag-to-reorder list (native HTML5 draggable,
≥44px handles, no swiping) plus a per-row move-up/move-down keyboard/AT path. Every
move — drag OR button — recomputes a dense manualRank 0..N-1 over the whole list and
issues ONE bulk PATCH /api/sort-results/[id]/items (S3a); the order updates
optimistically and reverts wholesale on failure (single atomic call = clean
rollback). 'Back to the computed order' DELETEs the overlay (optimistic revert by
computedRank). A finalized keepsake shows NO reorder affordance — reorder is a draft
activity — and instead offers 'Make a revision' (the supersede flow).

a11y: an sr-only role=status announces 'Moved {name} to position N of M'; keyboard
focus stays on the moved item's control (retained across the in-flight disabled
window); rows carry motion-reduce:transition-none. §4.4 framing lines name live
Standing as 'the current picture' and the draft as 'the keepsake you can shape'. All
copy is exported TONE constants with a register scan.

Tests: rerank-copy register scan; 12-case RerankPanel jsdom suite (drag→one PATCH,
optimistic+rollback, move-up/down swap PATCH, finalized guard + Make-a-revision,
role=status announce, ≥44px targets, reduced-motion, focus retention); page-level
draft-vs-finalized affordance assertions; an un-mocked e2e driving the move-up button
through the bulk endpoint → reload → persisted order (all 3 projects).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UQS4F4JxwFSyyMxHhVdSYz

* test(authz): register bulk re-rank PATCH/DELETE in the stranger-enumeration backstop (Epic S)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UQS4F4JxwFSyyMxHhVdSYz

* fix(results): fold Epic S review — refresh after reorder, curator-gate revision, in-tx finalized guard, within-tier hand-order, 1-indexed manualRank, dup-rid + copy/weight polish

- F-UX-I1: router.refresh() after a successful reorder/reset so the server-composed
  keepsake reflects the new order without a reload (optimistic + rollback kept).
- F-UX-I3: curator-gate the finalized "Make a revision" affordance (new canRevise
  prop, mirrors the SharePanel gate) so a non-curator can't fork another's keepsake.
- F-Data-I1: re-assert draft status INSIDE the reorder/reset transactions via a
  SELECT ... FOR UPDATE row lock (findByIdForUpdate) + ReorderFinalizedError → 409,
  closing the finalized-immutability TOCTOU.
- F-UX-I2: scope the hand-order list to the loved tier (what manualRank orders);
  Onward rows render read-only. Follow-up purses-9v1f.1 for cross-tier hand-order.
- F-Data-M1: write manualRank 1-indexed to share computedRank's 1..N space.
- F-Data-M2: reject duplicate rids in the reorder batch at the Zod boundary → 400.
- F-UX-M1: "Back to the computed order" → "Back to the suggested order".
- F-UX-M2: F5 heading "The ones you live with" → "The ones you've weighed in on".
- F-UX-M4: drop font-medium from the usage chip (Badge base font-semibold wins).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UQS4F4JxwFSyyMxHhVdSYz

* chore(epicS): CI wiring, usage-chip seed, doc + test alignment for merge

- ci.yml: add e2e/results-rerank.spec.ts to the results area→spec map so a
  results-only PR selects it (it never ran in CI before).
- seed: seedSortScenario records usage decisions (so the Standing usage chip
  renders on the draft + live Decide surfaces) and a finalized result carrying
  the usage snapshot; capture.ts adds the results-finalized surface.
- results-rerank.spec: correct to the shipped loved-only hand-order design —
  the reorder list holds the 2 loved rows (Onward excluded, cross-tier is
  purses-9v1f.1); assert the Onward item is not reorderable.
- Drop the redundant copy-ceremony tests (usage-chip-copy, rerank-copy): the
  register-scans/tautologies are covered by RerankPanel.test.tsx against real
  DOM (aria labels, role=status announcement).
- ARCHITECTURE: decision #29 (Standing usage chip + hand-order).
- Refresh graphify graph.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Tb3s1QSGtkTEuF18Euaqf6
